body:
Why old chatbots failed and AI chatbots work

Most people have used a website chatbot that only offered four buttons and replied “Sorry, I didn’t understand that” to everything else. Those rule-based bots frustrated customers because they could only handle the exact questions someone had scripted. AI chatbots are different. They understand free-text questions, cope with spelling mistakes and follow-up questions, and answer from the information you give them.

The result is a chat assistant that can actually resolve enquiries: explaining your services, checking whether you work in a suburb, comparing options, quoting approved prices and booking the next step. You can try one right now: open “Ask Crenosoft AI” in the corner of this page.

What our AI chatbots do

  • Answer questions about your services, pricing, process, opening hours and policies, using only your approved content.
  • Qualify and capture leads by asking your screening questions and sending details straight to your CRM.
  • Book appointments or calls by checking your calendar and confirming a time in the chat.
  • Handle common support requests such as order status, returns, account questions and how-to guides.
  • Hand over to a person with the conversation history when a customer asks, is upset or has a complex need.
  • Work across channels so the same assistant answers on your website, Messenger, WhatsApp and SMS.

Trained on your content, not the open internet

A business chatbot should never invent an answer. We build a knowledge base from your website, service pages, price lists, policies, product data and past email replies, and the chatbot answers from that material. Where it helps, it links to the source page so customers can read more. When the knowledge base doesn’t cover a question, the chatbot says so and offers to connect the customer with your team.

For larger document sets, such as technical manuals or internal policies for staff, the same approach scales into a full LLM and RAG knowledge-base assistant.

Rule-based chatbot vs AI chatbot

Rule-based chatbotCrenosoft AI chatbot
Understands free textOnly exact keywordsYes, including follow-up questions
Set-up effortEvery path scripted by handBuilt from your existing content
Keeps up to dateManual editsKnowledge base refreshed from your site
Takes actionsLimitedBooks, captures leads, updates CRM
Hands over to staffOften missingBuilt in, with full context

Guardrails that protect your brand

We set clear rules on what the chatbot can and cannot say. It won’t give medical, legal or financial advice, quote prices you haven’t approved or discuss competitors. It tells users they are chatting with an AI assistant, and every conversation is logged so you can review it. Before launch we test it against real customer questions and deliberate attempts to make it go off script.

Chat transcripts can include personal information, so data handling follows the Privacy Act 1988 and the OAIC’s guidance on commercially available AI products. The chatbot only asks for details it needs, and you choose how long transcripts are kept.

Measuring chatbot performance

Each month we report conversations handled, questions answered without a person, leads captured, bookings made and handovers. We also review a sample of conversations to find questions the chatbot couldn’t answer, then add that information to the knowledge base. Over time the chatbot handles more, and your team handles less of the repetitive work.

How we build your AI chatbot

  1. Free AI audit: we review your enquiry volumes and the questions customers ask most.
  2. Knowledge base: we gather and structure your content and agree the rules.
  3. Build and connect: we set up the chatbot, its channels and your CRM and calendar.
  4. Testing: your team tries real and awkward questions until it answers well.
  5. Launch and improve: usually two to three weeks after kick-off, with monthly reviews.

Want phone calls handled too? Pair your chatbot with an AI receptionist, or see all our AI agents.

Chatbots for Australian industries

Clinics use AI chatbots to answer questions about treatments, fees and Medicare or health fund rebates the clinic has approved, then book appointments. Real estate agencies use them to answer listing questions and book inspections after hours. Trades businesses use them to collect job details and photos before quoting. eCommerce stores use them for order tracking, sizing and returns. Each chatbot starts from the same core but is trained on that industry’s language and your own rules.
faqs: How long does it take to build an AI chatbot?
A website chatbot trained on your existing content usually goes live in two to three weeks. Chatbots that connect to several systems or channels can take four to six weeks, including testing.
Will the chatbot make up answers?

We design it to answer only from your approved knowledge base and to say when it doesn’t know. It links to sources where possible and offers to connect the customer with your team for anything it can’t answer.
Can the chatbot work on WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger?
Yes. The same AI assistant can answer on your website, Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp and SMS, so customers get consistent answers wherever they contact you.
How much does an AI chatbot cost in Australia?

Cost depends on the channels, integrations and conversation volume. We quote a fixed build price in AUD after a free audit, plus a monthly fee for hosting, AI usage, monitoring and knowledge-base updates.
